sections.h1: School Signs in New York City for Classrooms and Campus Buildings
sections.lead_html:
A school sign speaks to students, families, and visitors who may not know the building.

Vision Graphics designs and makes signage for schools in NYC, from classroom signs and hallway wayfinding to school pride graphics, as part of our interior signs in NYC range.

We plan installation around the school calendar and manage it through licensed partners.

sections.html:

sections.intro_html: Pride graphics give a school its identity on large walls and glass. Plan the artwork with the school, and keep daily information on separate surfaces.

items.title: Mascot and Values Walls
items.html: Large wall graphics can feature a mascot, a motto, or school values. See wall graphics in NYC for wall options.

items.title: Murals
items.html: Murals suit large walls in halls, gyms, and cafeterias. See murals for large-format options.

items.title: Window Graphics
items.html: Window graphics add school colors, hours, or messages to entrances and offices. See window graphics in NYC.

items.title: Mission and Values Signs
items.html: A mission or values sign sets a statement in a dimensional or printed format. See mission statement signs.

items.title: High School Graphics and Signage
items.html: High school graphics signage often combines team spirit, achievements, and wayfinding. Custom school signage starts with the approved name, colors, and logo, so one visual system keeps graphics and signs in agreement.

items.title: Student Photos and Names
items.html: Use student photos and names only with the permissions and approvals your school requires. Confirm rights before artwork is released.

sections.intro_html: Room signs need clear names and a plan for the applicable standards. The ADA Standards set the rules, and your design professional confirms what applies.

items.title: Permanent Room Signs
items.html: Permanent room signs need raised characters and Braille, where provided, under the ADA Standards. Classroom door signage with a room number and a name is common. See door signs in NYC.

items.title: Directional and Informational Signs
items.html: Directional and informational signs need only visual criteria: contrast, a non-glare finish, and legible characters. Placement still affects how well people find their way.

items.title: Updating Names
items.html: Room names change with programs and staff. Ask our team about updateable options.

items.title: Standards Review
items.html: Your school's design professional confirms the standards for each sign. We state the rules and do not certify compliance. See ADA signs in NYC.

sections.intro_html: Events change often, so plan them apart from permanent signs. School event signage works well when daily guidance stays clear underneath.

items.title: Open Houses and Graduations
items.html: Banners and display graphics mark open houses, orientations, and graduations. See banners in NYC.

items.title: Sports and Performances
items.html: Event banners and entry graphics support games, shows, and community nights. Plan hanging points and removal dates before printing.

items.title: Daily Guidance and Changing News
items.html: School communication signage works when permanent room and department signs stay readable beside event posters. Choose which surfaces change often, and keep names consistent.

sections.h2: Planning School Signage Around the Calendar
sections.intro_html: School projects work around the calendar, the approvals, and the building's access rules. These five points shape the schedule.

items.title: Summer and School Breaks
items.html: Summer and school breaks usually give installers the most open access. Tell us your dates early so the schedule fits, and ask about evenings and weekends.

items.title: Approvals and Content Ownership
items.html: Confirm who approves names, logos, photos, and student-related content. Gather your sign standards and facilities requirements before design starts.

items.title: How Schools Buy
items.html: NYC Public Schools buys through contracts and small purchases under its procurement rules. Colleges may use formal bids that list sign types and set insurance and reference requirements. Our team confirms the purchasing path your school uses.

items.title: Building Access and Clearance
items.html: Anyone working in NYC public school buildings may need background clearance under Chancellor's Regulation C-105. Tell us early, so our team can confirm the access steps for your building.

items.title: Insurance and Paperwork
items.html: We can provide a certificate of insurance upon request, and our team will confirm your school's requirements. Public and college projects may set insurance, wage, and subcontractor terms, so send them early.

sections.intro_html: School needs differ by type, size, and decision-making. These are the groups we plan for.

items.title: Independent and Private Schools
items.html: Independent and private schools set their own approvals, so name your approver early. Share brand standards and any donor or heritage details with the brief.

items.title: Charter Schools
items.html: Charter school signs often need to be ready for enrollment and open-house dates. Share your target dates early, so production and installation fit.

items.title: Colleges and Universities
items.html: University signage and college campus signs often cover many buildings and departments. Plan the sign types, floor plans, and review steps for the whole campus.

sections.after_html: Public school purchasing paths vary. Ask our team how your school buys.

items.title: Building Approval
items.html: Interior signs may require approval from the school or building management, and we prepare the drawings they ask for. Send any school or building sign rules early, so the drawings match them.

items.title: What to Send

items.q: Are you an approved vendor for NYC schools?
items.a_html: That depends on how your school buys. NYC Public Schools buys through contracts and small purchases under its procurement rules, and colleges may use formal bids. Tell us what your purchasing office requires, and our team confirms the paperwork we can provide.

items.q: Can you install during school breaks or after hours?
items.a_html: Yes. We schedule installs around your school's rules, including evenings, weekends, and school breaks. After-hours work can add labor charges, and we confirm them in your quote. Licensed installation partners handle the installation, and our project lead manages the schedule.

items.q: Are your classroom and room signs ADA compliant?
items.a_html: The ADA Standards set the rules for these signs. Permanent room signs need raised characters and Braille where provided, and directional signs need visual criteria. Your school's design professional confirms what applies, and our team discusses specifications with you.

items.q: How much does a school signage project usually cost?
items.a_html: Cost depends on the number of rooms, sign types, and sizes. Planning ranges are about $50 to $150 for standard indoor room and directional signs and $100 to $250 for corridor directionals. Wall graphics and banners are quoted by size, and your quote replaces these ranges.

items.q: Do you also do exterior signs and wall graphics for schools?
items.a_html: Yes. We make exterior signs and wall graphics for schools, and each has its own page. Exterior signs may need city permits, which our project lead plans with you. See exterior signs in NYC and wall graphics in NYC.

items.q: How do NYC schools buy signage?
items.a_html: NYC Public Schools buys through contracts and small purchases under its procurement rules. Colleges may use formal bids that list sign types and set reference and insurance terms. Private and charter schools set their own approval processes. Our team confirms the path your school uses.

items.q: Do installers need background clearance to work in a school?
items.a_html: They may. Chancellor's Regulation C-105 requires background clearance for people working in NYC public school buildings, and other schools may set their own checks. Tell us early, and our team confirms the access steps for your building.

items.q: Can signs use student photos or names?
items.a_html: Only with the permissions and approvals your school requires. Confirm rights for each photo and name before artwork is released. Tell us who approves the final design, so the drawing reaches the right person before production.

items.q: Can you update room signs when names change?
items.a_html: Often, with updateable components. They let you change a room or department name without replacing the whole sign. Our team confirms the options for your building and how to order replacements. Share your list of names so that we can plan those signs first.

items.q: Which sign companies work with schools in NYC?
items.a_html: Vision Graphics is a school signage company that designs and makes signs for NYC schools and campuses, with a 60-year history and production in Salt Lake City. Licensed installation partners install them, managed by one project lead. We serve all five boroughs. Send your location list, and our team replies with a drawing and a quote.
